clue.text: One's obliged to serve Tory lines

parts.note: a Tory is a Conservative, abbreviated CON
an actor's lines make up the script

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician is bound to deliver the party lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' reads as 'one is', so the definition is a person obliged to serve, as in the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone drafted by compulsory enlistment is required to serve in the military.

clue.text: Very nearly clear the charge for function

indicators.note: very nearly means the word for clear stops one letter short of complete

parts.note: clear, as in unobstructed, means open
a charge is a rate or fee

explanation.surface: Someone is told to settle nearly all of a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very nearly' drops the last letter N from OPEN, leaving OPE.
explanation.definitionFit: To function is to work or run, which is what a machine does when it operates.

clue.text: One who looks small — tinker?

parts.note: to tinker is to potter about aimlessly

explanation.surface: A question asks whether a short-sighted observer is a travelling tinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinker' looks like a noun, a mender of pots, but is used as the verb meaning to potter.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotter is an observer, a person who watches for something, such as trains or planes.

clue.text: Star's reading is poor and ultimately hesitant

indicators.note: poor suggests the word reading is badly done, so its letters are rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of the word hesitant

explanation.surface: An astronomer's measurement is unreliable and wavering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges READING to REDGIAN, and 'ultimately' adds T, the last letter of hesitant. 'Star's' is 'star is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A red giant is a large, cool, late-stage star with a reddish glow.

clue.text: The objective is to surface the road — understand?

parts.note: tar is spread to give a road its surface
to get something is to understand it

explanation.surface: A roadworks foreman asks whether the crew grasps the plan to resurface.
explanation.definitionFit: An objective is an aim or goal, something one sets out to hit.

clue.text: Differentiates between various garments

definitions.meaning: to differentiate between things is to tell them apart or divide them
individual items of clothing, such as skirts and tops, sold to be worn in different combinations

explanation.surface: Someone sorts through a pile of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide things is to distinguish them; and clothes sold as single pieces to mix and match are a fashion-trade category.

clue.text: Characteristic found in ship's difficult situation

indicators.note: found in says the characteristic is placed inside the letters for ship

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the standard abbreviation for a ship
a characteristic is a trait

explanation.surface: A personality quirk shows itself when a vessel runs into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Straits' in the plural, as in 'dire straits', means a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in straits means being in trouble or hardship, often financial.

clue.text: Wrote hurriedly and withdrew

definitions.meaning: to scrawl a note quickly on paper
pulled out of a race or contest before it began

explanation.surface: Someone jotted a note in haste and then pulled out.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasty writing is a scrawl or scribble; a horse removed from a race before the start is said to be taken out of it.

clue.text: Pate (sic) that's free of pathological micro-organisms

annotationWithheld.why: Pate (sic) that's free of pathological micro-organisms: anagram of PATE SIC, but the only anagram indicator is 'free', which is also needed in the definition 'free of pathological micro-organisms', so one word does two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Pate (sic) that's free of pathological micro-organisms

clue.text: Endorses merchandise that's not perfect

definitions.meaning: to back or support a motion formally
factory goods with minor flaws sold cheaply

explanation.surface: A celebrity puts their name to a range of flawed goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Backing a motion at a meeting is the verb sense; goods with flaws sold at a discount are the noun sense.

clue.text: Had an argument in returning from the city

indicators.note: returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone quarrelled on the way home from town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals that the letters ADANARG are tucked inside 'Had an argument'; 'returning' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Granada is a city in Andalusia, southern Spain, home of the Alhambra.

clue.text: Leave free starters of goujons, and eat game bird

parts.note: to leave someone is to part from them
to free someone of a thing is to rid them of it

indicators.note: starters means the opening letters of the words goujons and eat

explanation.surface: A diner is told to skip the fish-strip appetisers and have the game course.
explanation.walkthrough: Goujons are strips of fish or chicken fried in breadcrumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a plump ground-dwelling bird shot for sport and food.

clue.text: Spiritual guide's cheese wrapped by young lady

indicators.note: wrapped by says the cheese sits inside the word for young lady

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl or young woman
Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: A girl hides some soft cheese belonging to her mentor.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabriel is the archangel who acts as messenger and guide in Jewish, Christian and Islamic tradition.

clue.text: Almost come down in Greek pond

indicators.note: in says the shortened word goes inside the word for Greek

parts.note: Attic means of Attica or Athens, so Greek

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped from the word for come down

parts.note: a plane coming down is said to land

explanation.surface: An aircraft nearly touches down in a pool in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims LAND to LAN; 'the pond' is a jokey name for the Atlantic Ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossing the pond is a humorous idiom for crossing the ocean between Britain and America.

clue.text: Cell nineteen's case — full of foreign money

indicators.note: full of says the currency is packed inside the outer letters
case means the outside letters of the word nineteen, which enclose the rest

parts.note: the euro is the currency of much of continental Europe

explanation.surface: A box belonging to a number is stuffed with overseas cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' gives the first and last letters of nineteen, N and N, which go around EURO.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerve cell that transmits electrical signals in the brain and nervous system.

clue.text: Went to sleep, having agreed to execute posh bloke

parts.note: nodding the head shows agreement

indicators.note: to execute is to behead, so the first letter is cut off the word for posh bloke

parts.note: a toff is an upper-class man

explanation.surface: Someone dozed off after consenting to have an aristocrat killed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'execute' is a beheading: TOFF loses its head, T, to leave OFF. Toff is British slang for a posh person.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping into sleep, especially without meaning to, while sitting up.

clue.text: Socrates managed to cross one and got cast out

indicators.note: to cross means the letter for one goes across the middle of the rearranged name
managed suggests the name Socrates is handled and reworked into new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The philosopher contrived to upset someone and was banished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' rearranges SOCRATES to OSTRACSE; 'to cross' puts I inside it. Fittingly, ostracism began in Socrates' Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude someone from a group or society, shunning them.

clue.text: Where the shop keeps silver?

indicators.note: keeps says the word for shop holds the silver inside it

parts.note: a shop is a store
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A question about where a shop puts its valuables.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: storage is where a shop keeps its stock, silver included.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockroom or holding space is where goods are kept until needed.

clue.text: Most of the factory supports adventurous scheme

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece that supports another sits below it

parts.note: game means willing and adventurous, as in game for anything

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped from the word for factory

parts.note: a factory is a plant

explanation.surface: A works sponsors a daring project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' trims PLANT to PLAN; 'supports' puts it under GAME in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy or plan of action worked out in advance.

clue.text: Fierce sheep sound out of breath

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
to pant is to breathe hard and noisily

explanation.surface: An aggressive ewe's mate wheezes heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrestrained and violent; a heraldic lion reared up to attack is described this way.

clue.text: Get up to listen to a broadcast

indicators.note: listen to means the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: to send is to broadcast, so a broadcast becomes a send

explanation.surface: Someone is told to rise and tune in to a programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a send' said out loud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise or climb; to go upward.

clue.text: Preserve farewell musical work

parts.note: food is preserved by sealing it in a can
ta-ta is an informal British goodbye

explanation.surface: A goodbye song is kept for posterity.
explanation.definitionFit: A choral composition with solos and chorus, often sacred, as by Bach.

clue.text: Profit on dance goes to sport

parts.note: net profit is earnings after costs
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Money made from a dance is given to an athletics club.
explanation.definitionFit: A team game, played mostly by women, in which goals are scored by throwing through a high hoop.

clue.text: Verbal onslaught from desperate-sounding family group

indicators.note: sounding means the word for desperate is heard, not spelt

parts.note: dire means desperate or dreadful
a tribe is a group of related families

explanation.surface: A rant comes from a clan in a bad way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dire' in a non-rhotic British accent is said like DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter, abusive tirade or harangue.

clue.text: Gamble, accepting request for container

indicators.note: accepting says the word for gamble takes the request inside it

parts.note: a bet is a gamble
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A punter takes a bet and asks for a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A woven holder for carrying or storing things.

clue.text: Every other tent a real disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in chaos, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A camping trip goes badly wrong for every second tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurring in turn, one in two, as in alternate days.

clue.text: Pictures of Parisian with old people in Scotland

parts.note: de is French for of
the Picts were an ancient people of northern Scotland

explanation.surface: Photographs from a Frenchman showing Scotland's ancient inhabitants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pictures' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray or represent something in a drawing or in words.

clue.text: Animals an accountant found in the mountains

indicators.note: found in says the letters go inside the mountains

parts.note: the Alps are the great European mountain range
an is the indefinite article, A
CA is chartered accountant

explanation.surface: An auditor comes across some livestock on a hike in the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: Domesticated South American camelids related to the llama, kept for their wool.

clue.text: Financial penalties require case of severe and skilful manipulation

parts.note: fines are money penalties

indicators.note: case of means the outer letters of the word severe, enclosing the rest

explanation.surface: Penalties call for tough handling and deftness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' gives S and E, the first and last letters of severe.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicate skill and subtlety in handling a situation.

clue.text: Go and propose — get a revolver!

parts.note: a go in a game is a turn
to table a motion is to propose it for discussion

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to make a proposal and then pick up a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a revolver' is not a gun but something that revolves, a record deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating platform, such as a record player's deck, which goes round and round.
